title: Restriction stability of degree-zero supported model hull membership
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring on profinite sets, and on a scheme $T$ let $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Use ordinary derived categories and the small pro-etale sites and fixed indexing universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal G_T$ be the supported model hull [def-sfb-supported-model-hull], namely the intersection of full replete triangulated classes containing supported finite scalar local models in degree zero and closed under retracts, small products and termwise colimits of strict filtered diagrams with a common lower bound. Let $W,T$ be quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $r:W\to T$ be weakly etale, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [sk-def-pe-morphisms, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For every actual module $N\in\mathcal A_T$ with $N[0]\in\mathcal G_T$, one has $(r^*N)[0]\in\mathcal G_W$, where $r^*$ is the actual exact coefficient-compatible module inverse image [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. No coefficient admissibility, covering, affine or weak-contractibility hypothesis is needed. Empty schemes, zero coefficients, zero modules and the identity map are included.

proof.text: For a qcqs site arrow $r:W\to T$, the site of $W$ is the localization of that of $T$. On section-ring modules its inverse image is restriction: $(U,s)\mapsto M(U)$; identify its coefficient ring with $\Lambda_W$ and transport along the exact internal/section-module equivalences. This is an exact functor preserving sheaf products (the displayed section formula) and all colimits (the module pullback adjunction). Applying it termwise therefore preserves products in the derived categories by the termwise-product theorem, and takes a strict filtered diagram with common termwise lower bound to one with the same bound. It preserves shifts and triangles by exactness, and preserves retract diagrams by functoriality.

proof.text: All schemes of a support chain are qcqs: an open arrow is quasi-compact by hypothesis, while a closed subscheme of a qcqs scheme has a finite affine cover with pairwise intersections closed in the ambient quasi-compact intersections. Apply closed-subset quasi-compactness and the affine-cover criterion inductively. Base-change each arrow in a support chain along $r$. The resulting arrows are again quasi-compact opens or closed immersions with quasi-compact open complement: use qcqs permanence for quasi-compactness and the open/closed base-change squares for the immersion properties. The canonical module base-change isomorphisms give $r^*JL\cong J' r_W^*L$. Pulling back the cover trivializing $L$ gives a cover trivializing $r_W^*L$ by the same finitely presented scalar modules; the scalar extension formula is unchanged by restriction. Thus generators pull back to generators. By the preceding step the replete class of objects $K$ such that $r^*K\in\mathcal G_W$ has every closure property defining $\mathcal G_T$. Intersecting gives $r^*(\mathcal G_T)\subseteq\mathcal G_W$. This is a direct use of the defining intersection, not descent of hull-membership.
